correctness.rationale: The exact silhouette criterion follows from the unique linear relation among three projected generator pairs; the six-vertex event is strict triangle inequalities on coordinates in the V basis. Their eight sign-cones have two same-sign and six mixed-sign spherical areas, evaluated from explicit rays using a standard atan2 trihedral solid-angle formula with its negative-denominator branch. The two half-angles have explicit derivatives, giving the closed-form probability and exact sign of its derivative for every h>0. The only stationary point is h=1/sqrt(2), the regular octahedron, with second derivative 8sqrt(2)/(9pi). Both endpoint limits and null degeneracies are handled. Standalone direct 2D hull sampling and independently recomputed solid angles passed at five heights; finite tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The essential new claim is a complete exact height law together with the unique global minimum and sharp quadratic stability in a nonorthogonal triangular-antiprism deformation. Prior regular octahedron probability and general solid-angle/expected-shadow identities are expressly not new. Primary full text gives no prior antiprism height optimization. A published triaxial orthogonal-axes theorem instead proves the regular member uniquely maximizes in a different deformation family, whose nonregular members cannot be the present antiprisms because their generator dot products are nonzero. A published uniform-antiprism X-ray result concerns a different invariant. Historical priority remains provisional, especially for older angle-sum formulations.
residual_risks: Prior general angle-sum identities imply an implicit silhouette probability; a historically known optimized nonorthogonal one-parameter specialization, if found, would defeat originality.
Searchable sources and published records do not guarantee historical uniqueness, especially older integral geometry and octahedral projection treatments.
The nonorthogonal family is strictly smaller than all affine octahedra; the theorem does not settle an all-affine global extremum.

value.rationale: For a natural equilateral-base nonorthogonal deformation of an octahedron, the theorem supplies a complete Haar shadow-vertex probability, a unique sharp minimizer, and an exact quadratic shape stability constant. The regular octahedron plays the opposite role to its known maximum among perpendicular-axis stretches, revealing structurally different silhouette behavior under angular versus length anisotropy. The novel extremal phenomenon is not a textbook count, a renaming, or a mere restatement of the known regular-octahedron constant.
